### CVE-2026-34769 — Electron: Renderer command-line switch injection via undocumented commandLineSwitches webPreference
- Assigner: GitHub_M | Published: 2026-04-03 | Updated: 2026-07-15 | Max CVSS: 7.8
- CWE: CWE-88 CWE-88: Improper Neutralization of Argument Delimiters in a Command ('Argument Injection'); CWE-912 CWE-912: Hidden Functionality; CWE-88 Improper Neutralization of Argument Delimiters in a Command ('Argument Injection')
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 7.8 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total
- CVSS 3.1 (redhat-SADP): 7.7 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H`

Electron is a framework for writing cross-platform desktop applications using JavaScript, HTML and CSS. Prior to versions 38.8.6, 39.8.0, 40.7.0, and 41.0.0-beta.8, an undocumented commandLineSwitches webPreference allowed arbitrary switches to be appended to the renderer process command line. Apps that construct webPreferences by spreading untrusted configuration objects may inadvertently allow an attacker to inject switches that disable renderer sandboxing or web security controls. Apps are only affected if they construct webPreferences from external or untrusted input without an allowlist. Apps that use a fixed, hardcoded webPreferences object are not affected. This issue has been patched in versions 38.8.6, 39.8.0, 40.7.0, and 41.0.0-beta.8.

Affected:
- electron / electron: affected < 38.8.6; affected >= 39.0.0-alpha.1, < 39.8.0; affected >= 40.0.0-alpha.1, < 40.7.0; affected >= 41.0.0-alpha.1, < 41.0.0-beta.8

### CVE-2026-34770 — Electron: Use-after-free in PowerMonitor on Windows and macOS
- Assigner: GitHub_M | Published: 2026-04-03 | Updated: 2026-04-08 | Max CVSS: 7
- CWE: CWE-416 CWE-416: Use After Free
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 7 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

Electron is a framework for writing cross-platform desktop applications using JavaScript, HTML and CSS. Prior to versions 38.8.6, 39.8.1, 40.8.0, and 41.0.0-beta.8, apps that use the powerMonitor module may be vulnerable to a use-after-free. After the native PowerMonitor object is garbage-collected, the associated OS-level resources (a message window on Windows, a shutdown handler on macOS) retain dangling references. A subsequent session-change event (Windows) or system shutdown (macOS) dereferences freed memory, which may lead to a crash or memory corruption. All apps that access powerMonitor events (suspend, resume, lock-screen, etc.) are potentially affected. The issue is not directly renderer-controllable. This issue has been patched in versions 38.8.6, 39.8.1, 40.8.0, and 41.0.0-beta.8.

Affected:
- electron / electron: affected < 38.8.6; affected >= 39.0.0-alpha.1, < 39.8.1; affected >= 40.0.0-alpha.1, < 40.8.0; affected >= 41.0.0-alpha.1, < 41.0.0-beta.8

### CVE-2026-34771 — Electron: Use-after-free in WebContents fullscreen, pointer-lock, and keyboard-lock permission callbacks
- Assigner: GitHub_M | Published: 2026-04-03 | Updated: 2026-07-15 | Max CVSS: 7.5
- CWE: CWE-416 CWE-416: Use After Free; CWE-364 Signal Handler Race Condition
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 7.5 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total
- CVSS 3.1 (redhat-SADP): 7.5 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`

Electron is a framework for writing cross-platform desktop applications using JavaScript, HTML and CSS. Prior to versions 38.8.6, 39.8.0, 40.7.0, and 41.0.0-beta.8, apps that register an asynchronous session.setPermissionRequestHandler() may be vulnerable to a use-after-free when handling fullscreen, pointer-lock, or keyboard-lock permission requests. If the requesting frame navigates or the window closes while the permission handler is pending, invoking the stored callback dereferences freed memory, which may lead to a crash or memory corruption. Apps that do not set a permission request handler, or whose handler responds synchronously, are not affected. This issue has been patched in versions 38.8.6, 39.8.0, 40.7.0, and 41.0.0-beta.8.

Affected:
- electron / electron: affected < 38.8.6; affected >= 39.0.0-alpha.1, < 39.8.0; affected >= 40.0.0-alpha.1, < 40.7.0; affected >= 41.0.0-alpha.1, < 41.0.0-beta.8

### CVE-2026-34774 — Electron: Use-after-free in offscreen child window paint callback
- Assigner: GitHub_M | Published: 2026-04-03 | Updated: 2026-07-15 | Max CVSS: 8.1
- CWE: CWE-416 CWE-416: Use After Free; CWE-825 Expired Pointer Dereference
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 8.1 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total
- CVSS 3.1 (redhat-SADP): 8.1 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`

Electron is a framework for writing cross-platform desktop applications using JavaScript, HTML and CSS. Prior to versions 39.8.1, 40.7.0, and 41.0.0, apps that use offscreen rendering and allow child windows via window.open() may be vulnerable to a use-after-free. If the parent offscreen WebContents is destroyed while a child window remains open, subsequent paint frames on the child dereference freed memory, which may lead to a crash or memory corruption. Apps are only affected if they use offscreen rendering (webPreferences.offscreen: true) and their setWindowOpenHandler permits child windows. Apps that do not use offscreen rendering, or that deny child windows, are not affected. This issue has been patched in versions 39.8.1, 40.7.0, and 41.0.0.

Affected:
- electron / electron: affected < 39.8.1; affected >= 40.0.0-alpha.1, < 40.7.0; affected >= 41.0.0-alpha.1, < 41.0.0

### CVE-2026-34780 — Electron: Context Isolation bypass via contextBridge VideoFrame transfer
- Assigner: GitHub_M | Published: 2026-04-04 | Updated: 2026-07-15 | Max CVSS: 8.4
- CWE: CWE-668 CWE-668: Exposure of Resource to Wrong Sphere; CWE-1188 CWE-1188: Insecure Default Initialization of Resource; CWE-501 Trust Boundary Violation
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 8.4 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total
- CVSS 3.1 (redhat-SADP): 8 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H`

Electron is a framework for writing cross-platform desktop applications using JavaScript, HTML and CSS. From versions 39.0.0-alpha.1 to before 39.8.0, 40.0.0-alpha.1 to before 40.7.0, and 41.0.0-alpha.1 to before 41.0.0-beta.8, apps that pass VideoFrame objects (from the WebCodecs API) across the contextBridge are vulnerable to a context isolation bypass. An attacker who can execute JavaScript in the main world (for example, via XSS) can use a bridged VideoFrame to gain access to the isolated world, including any Node.js APIs exposed to the preload script. Apps are only affected if a preload script returns, resolves, or passes a VideoFrame object to the main world via contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld(). Apps that do not bridge VideoFrame objects are not affected. This issue has been patched in versions 39.8.0, 40.7.0, and 41.0.0-beta.8.

- electron / electron: affected >= 39.0.0-alpha.1, < 39.8.0; affected >= 40.0.0-alpha.1, < 40.7.0; affected >= 41.0.0-alpha.1, < 41.0.0-beta.8

### CVE-2026-70601 — Electron: Context isolation bypass via Function.prototype.bind hijack
- Assigner: GitHub_M | Published: 2026-08-05 | Updated: 2026-08-05 | Max CVSS: 7.5

- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 7.5 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:L/A:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=partial

Electron is a framework for writing cross-platform desktop applications using JavaScript, HTML and CSS. Prior to 39.8.9, 40.9.2, 41.2.2, and 42.0.0-beta.5, apps that expose Promise-returning functions to web content via contextBridge may be vulnerable to a context isolation bypass. Untrusted web content could obtain access to the isolated preload world and, through it, every capability the preload script has. In renderers without a sandbox, or with nodeIntegration enabled, this may escalate to Node.js access. Apps are affected if they expose Promise-returning functions via contextBridge, the standard pattern for wrapping ipcRenderer.invoke, in windows that load untrusted content. This issue is fixed in versions 39.8.9, 40.9.2, 41.2.2, and 42.0.0-beta.5.

### CVE-2026-70604 — Electron: Custom protocol with supportFetchAPI but not corsEnabled allows cross-origin reads
- Assigner: GitHub_M | Published: 2026-08-05 | Updated: 2026-08-05 | Max CVSS: 7.4
- CWE: CWE-942 CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 7.4 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:N/A:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=partial

Electron is a framework for writing cross-platform desktop applications using JavaScript, HTML and CSS. Prior to 39.8.10, 40.9.3, 41.4.0, and 42.0.0, a custom scheme registered with supportFetchAPI: true but without corsEnabled: true was not subject to CORS enforcement. A page loaded from a remote origin could therefore fetch() or XMLHttpRequest that scheme cross-origin and read the full response body, rather than the read being blocked. Apps that serve sensitive data from such a scheme and load remote or untrusted content in a renderer are affected. This issue is fixed in versions 39.8.10, 40.9.3, 41.4.0, and 42.0.0.

Affected:
- electron / electron: affected < 39.8.10; affected >= 40.0.0-alpha.1, < 40.9.3; affected >= 41.0.0-alpha.1, < 41.4.0; affected >= 42.0.0-alpha.1, < 42.0.0

### CVE-2026-102673 — Electron drops inherited HTML sandbox restrictions for popups opened through OpenURLFromTab
- Assigner: GitHub_M | Published: 2026-09-29 | Updated: 2026-09-30 | Max CVSS: 8.2
- CWE: CWE-346 CWE-346: Origin Validation Error; CWE-693 CWE-693: Protection Mechanism Failure
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 8.2 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:L/A:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=partial

Electron is a framework for writing cross-platform desktop applications using JavaScript, HTML and CSS. Prior to 41.10.4, 42.5.2, and 43.0.0, popups opened from a sandboxed iframe through Electron's OpenURLFromTab navigation path, including links using target="_blank" or a middle-click, did not receive the inherited HTML sandbox restrictions. An untrusted iframe using the allow-scripts allow-popups configuration could therefore open a popup with the embedding application's full origin, exposing that origin's cookies, storage, and same-origin scripting capabilities. Applications that do not embed untrusted content in sandboxed iframes are not affected. This issue is fixed in versions 41.10.4, 42.5.2, and 43.0.0.

Affected:
- electron / electron: affected < 41.10.4; affected >= 42.0.0-alpha.1, < 42.5.2; affected >= 43.0.0-alpha.1, < 43.0.0

Prior to 41.10.6, 42.9.2, 43.4.1, and 44.0.0-beta.5, windows opened from a sandboxed top-level document did not inherit that document's active HTML sandbox restrictions. - CVSS 3.1 (cna): 8.3 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

Electron is a framework for writing cross-platform desktop applications using JavaScript, HTML and CSS. Prior to 41.10.6, 42.9.2, 43.4.1, and 44.0.0-beta.5, an Electron <webview> guest could enable nodeIntegrationInWorker for its Web Workers even when the unsandboxed embedder had Node.js integration disabled, allowing untrusted guest content to create a Node-enabled worker with more privilege than the embedder granted. Applications that do not enable the <webview> tag or that keep the embedder sandboxed are not affected. This issue is fixed in versions 41.10.6, 42.9.2, 43.4.1, and 44.0.0-beta.5.

Affected:
- electron / electron: affected < 41.10.6; affected >= 42.0.0-alpha.1, < 42.9.2; affected >= 43.0.0-alpha.1, < 43.4.1; affected >= 44.0.0-alpha.1, < 44.0.0-beta.5

### CVE-2026-102677 — Electron: Sandboxed preload code cache can be poisoned by a compromised renderer
- Assigner: GitHub_M | Published: 2026-09-29 | Updated: 2026-10-02 | Max CVSS: 7.8
- CWE: CWE-20 CWE-20: Improper Input Validation; CWE-345 CWE-345: Insufficient Verification of Data Authenticity
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 7.8 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

Electron is a framework for writing cross-platform desktop applications using JavaScript, HTML and CSS. From 42.3.3 until 42.10.0, 43.5.0, and 44.0.0-beta.6, Electron's sandboxed preload code cache did not verify that a cached entry matched the preload it was served for. A compromised renderer could write attacker-controlled cache data and cause Electron to reuse it for a later load, executing the renderer's code in the more privileged preload context. The issue affects applications that load untrusted content. This issue is fixed in versions 42.10.0, 43.5.0, and 44.0.0-beta.6.

Affected:
- electron / electron: affected >= 42.3.3, < 42.10.0; affected >= 43.0.0-beta.1, < 43.5.0; affected >= 44.0.0-alpha.1, < 44.0.0-beta.6

### CVE-2026-115570 — Electron: Mitigation for compromised eMudhra intermediate certificates
- Assigner: GitHub_M | Published: 2026-10-23 | Updated: 2026-10-23 | Max CVSS: 7.4
- CWE: CWE-299 CWE-299: Improper Check for Certificate Revocation
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 7.4 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

Electron is a framework for writing cross-platform desktop applications using JavaScript, HTML and CSS. Prior to 42.11.16, 43.8.1, 44.9.1, and 45.0.0-beta.6, Electron does not block compromised eMudhra intermediate certificates in Chromium networking, Node.js tls, Node.js https, or Node.js fetch. An attacker who holds a certificate issued through one of these intermediates and can intercept network traffic can impersonate a TLS server to an affected application. This issue is fixed in versions 42.11.16, 43.8.1, 44.9.1, and 45.0.0-beta.6.

Affected:
- electron / electron: affected >= 45.0.0-alpha.1, < 45.0.0-beta.6; affected >= 44.0.0-alpha.1, < 44.9.1; affected >= 43.0.0-alpha.1, < 43.8.1; affected < 42.11.16

### CVE-2026-134316 — @better-auth/electron before 1.7.16 Auth Secret Disclosure and Two-Factor Bypass
- Assigner: VulnCheck | Published: 2026-11-21 | Updated: 2026-11-23 | Max CVSS: 8.6
- CWE: CWE-201 Insertion of Sensitive Information Into Sent Data
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 8.6 HIGH `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:L/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 8.1 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

@better-auth/electron 1.5.0-beta.12 before 1.7.16 and 1.8.0-beta.0 before 1.8.0-beta.5 accepts any validly signed value as its transfer cookie and returns the full endpoint context, including the auth secret and social provider client secrets, in sign-in responses. Authenticated users can obtain these secrets to forge sessions as other users. Attackers knowing a password can exchange desktop authorization codes issued before two-factor verification to bypass the second factor.

Affected:
- better-auth / electron: affected 1.5.0-beta.12 <1.7.16 (semver); unaffected 1.7.16 (semver)
- better-auth / electron: affected 1.8.0-beta.0 <1.8.0-beta.5 (semver); unaffected 1.8.0-beta.5 (semver)

Credits: octane-security-team; shbhmantil
